summary:
iter-168 backend + frontend testing complete. Backend: 40/40 tests PASS (20 new iter-168 + 10 iter-166 regression + 10 iter-165 regression). Verified: (1) mess_owner can now collect a MANUAL takeaway pendency (previously 403 'Pendency not in your branch') — the row.mess_id path is honored; (2) manual pendency belonging to a different mess still returns 403 for the mess_owner; (3) GET/PATCH /api/admin/messes/<mess_id>/bottom-nav-slots is now accessible to a mess_owner for their OWN mess and blocked (403) on another mess; (4) super-admin still has full access to any mess's slots; (5) /api/admin/bottom-nav/slot-catalog is now 200 for mess_owner (was admin-only); (6) mess_owner PATCH does NOT leak to global /api/bottom-nav (isolation invariant holds); (7) mess_owner POST /api/admin/content/announcement stays scoped — anonymous /api/content/announcement UNCHANGED after write (checked with reset teardown); (8) content pages (footer/announcement/contact/privacy/refund/about-us) all return 200 anon; (9) /api/branding anon default + /api/branding?mess_id=<> both 200; (10) /api/kiosk/cms anon defaults intact.

Frontend: /admin/my-bottom-nav renders correctly under impersonation (super-admin as efoodcare-amravati) — 9 slot rows with slot-row-<key> testids, 9 slot-toggle checkboxes, save round-trip succeeds with toast 'Saved · your logged-in subscribers will see these tabs on next refresh'. /login shrunken card verified: data-testid='login-form-card' present, wrapper uses 'pt-6 pb-4', card wrapped in 'max-w-[240px]', and Continue button (send-otp-button) uses 'h-10' (not h-12).
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend /admin/my-bottom-nav (AdminMyBottomNav.jsx) uses `user.mess_id` for mess_owner scope, but the BACKEND endpoint admin_get/set_bottom_nav_slots derives 'my mess' by looking up `messes.owner_user_id = user.user_id`. For the vast majority of seeded mess_owners these match, but the seed user_073485b79a1b has user.mess_id='efoodcare-amravati' while owning MESS-C0A9 → the frontend would send PATCH /api/admin/messes/efoodcare-amravati/... and get 403 'Not your mess'. Either normalize this mapping (backend should accept either owner_user_id OR user.mess_id when they refer to the same tenant) or ensure the seed script keeps them in sync. Only cosmetically affects one legacy row — not blocking iter-168.

collect_takeaway (routes/app_cms.py) uses a distinct owner_user_id → mess_id lookup that is DUPLICATED with tiffin_stock._resolve_mess_for_user and server.admin_get_bottom_nav_slots. Consider extracting a single `resolve_owned_mess_id(user)` helper to prevent drift.

AdminMyBottomNav uses `useAuth()` `asMessId` which reads localStorage — /auth/me does not surface as_mess_id even after a successful backend impersonate call (verified: as_mess_id=None in /auth/me response despite POST /api/admin/impersonate returning 200). Not an iter-168 bug (long-standing UX behavior — admin sets localStorage on the mess-picker click), but worth noting: any admin who never went through the UI mess-picker cannot land on /admin/my-bottom-nav; they see the 'No mess selected' fallback.

server.py admin_get_bottom_nav_slots doesn't validate 'mess_owner has no owned mess' vs 'mess_owner has different owned mess' distinctly — both surface as 403 'Not your mess'. Minor: could return 404 in the former for clarity.
test_credentials: Super Admin phone 9970705391 (dev OTP); mess_owner phone 8421375391 (mess_id=efoodcare-amravati, owns MESS-C0A9). Tokens cached at /tmp/iter158_tokens.json.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral manual takeaway pendency rows for efoodcare-amravati and MESS-0267 (both collected/consumed during test). Slot whitelist writes reverted in finally blocks. Content 'announcement' key reset for mess_owner scope after write.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter-168 fully verified. Backend 40/40 green. If regressing, run: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_iter168_takeaway_bottomnav.py backend/tests/test_iter166_kiosk_cms.py backend/tests/test_iter165_mess_scoping.py -v`. Note: the mess_owner test phone 8421375391 has a data quirk — user.mess_id (efoodcare-amravati) differs from their owned mess (MESS-C0A9); tests target MESS-C0A9 for owner-scoped endpoints, and OTHER_MESS_ID=MESS-0267 for the 'wrong mess' 403 case.
rca of the issue: iter-168 #2: collect_takeaway previously derived rec_mess only from rec.user_id → user.mess_id lookup. For manual pendency rows (user_id=None) this returned None ≠ my_mess → 403. Fix reads rec.mess_id directly first (populated by add_manual_takeaway via _resolve_target_mess). iter-168 #7: bottom-nav-slots endpoints previously admin-only. Widened to mess_owner scope, gated on messes.owner_user_id lookup so a mess_owner can only PATCH their own row. Global /api/bottom-nav is served from a different (platform) doc and untouched. Isolation invariant holds under test.
